# gheasy


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

gheasy has four modules, and most projects only need one or two of them.

`gheasy.workflow` writes GitHub Actions workflows. A workflow is a YAML
file under `.github/workflows/` that tells GitHub which jobs to run on a
push, a pull request or a release. You describe it with chained Python
calls, and gheasy writes the YAML. You never write or indent YAML by
hand.

`gheasy.core` keeps a project’s CI settings in one file,
`.gheasy/config.json`, and generates the workflow, git hooks, Git LFS
rules and GitHub secrets from it. It also provides the `gheasy` command
line tool.

`gheasy.repo` reads and changes a local Git checkout. Before any change
that could lose work, such as a merge, a rebase or a reset, it records a
safepoint: the commit the branch pointed at and a snapshot of your
uncommitted changes. One call restores both.

`gheasy.repos` works across many checkouts at once, for a folder that
holds several repositories you work on together.

## Install

``` bash
pip install gheasy
```

## Generate a CI workflow

For a Python project that uses uv,
[`uv_ci`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/workflow.html#uv_ci)
returns a complete CI workflow. It runs on every push and pull request
to [`main`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#main),
installs dependencies with `uv sync --frozen`, runs ruff, and then runs
pytest. `lint_cmd=None`, as here, leaves out the lint job. `to_yaml`
returns the YAML text. `save('.github/workflows/ci.yml')` writes it to
the path where GitHub looks for workflows.

``` python
from gheasy.workflow import uv_ci
print(uv_ci("ci", lint_cmd=None).to_yaml())
```

    name: ci
    on:
      push:
        branches:
          - main
      pull_request:
        branches:
          - main
    jobs:
      test:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - name: Checkout
            uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - name: Setup uv
            uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
          - name: Install dependencies
            run: uv sync --frozen
          - name: Test
            run: uv run pytest

## Inspect a local repository

[`GitRepo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#gitrepo)
wraps one local checkout.
[`GitRepo.at`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#gitrepo.at)
takes the repository root or any file or folder inside it, and finds the
root. `info` returns everything an editor’s Git panel shows, in one
dictionary. The dictionary holds the current branch, the number of
commits the branch is ahead of and behind its upstream (the remote
branch it tracks), the local and remote branches, the remotes,
uncommitted changes, tags, stashes, any merge or rebase in progress,
whether the repository’s content filters can run, and the 12 most recent
safepoints. `info` caches its result for a short time. `brief` returns
one row with the branch, ahead and behind counts, uncommitted counts,
the last commit and the commits since the last tag. Use `brief` for a
status bar or a prompt.

``` python
from gheasy.repo import GitRepo
repo = GitRepo.at('.')
status = repo.info()
status['branch'], status['clean'], status['ahead'], status['behind']
```

## Preview before changing history

A merge can stop on conflicts, and a rebase rewrites your commits.
`divergence` shows what each would do before you run either. It compares
the current branch with its upstream and rehearses a fast-forward, a
merge, a rebase and a reset without performing any of them. It reports
which are available, which would conflict, and which one it recommends.
`fetch=True` fetches from the remote first. `merge_preview` reports a
proposed merge with the branch you name. `rebase_preview` reports a
proposed rebase onto the branch you name.

None of these methods change your branches, the index or the files on
disk. They use `git merge-tree`, which computes the result of a merge
without checking anything out.

``` python
preview = repo.divergence(fetch=True)
preview['relation'], preview['recommended'], preview['options']

repo.rebase_preview('origin/main')
```

## Change the repository with a way back

These methods record a safepoint before they run: `checkout`, `commit`,
`pull`, `merge`, `rebase`, `cherry_pick`, `revert`, `reset`, `sync`,
`stash_pop` and `stash_apply`. Each returns a dictionary with a
one-sentence `summary` of what happened and an `undo` token.
`undo(token)` restores the branch, the commit and the uncommitted work
as they were.

`sync` carries out one of the options `divergence` offered:
`fast-forward`, `merge`, `rebase` or `reset`. The default is `rebase`.
Call `divergence`, read `recommended`, and pass it to `sync`, as the
last line here does. `recommended` is an empty string when the branch is
identical to its upstream or ahead of it. Pass `sync` a real option in
that case, or skip the call.

``` python
result = repo.checkout('feature')
print(result['summary'])
repo.undo(result['undo'])

repo.sync(preview['recommended'])
```

## Review branches and commits

`review(base, head)` shows what a branch changed: each file with its
added and deleted line counts, the commits, and totals. It compares
`head` with the merge base, the last commit the two branches share.
Commits added to `base` after the branch split off do not appear as
changes of the branch. `review` does not load file contents.
`review_file(base, head, path)` loads the two versions of one file and
the patch between them when you call it. `commit_review` and
`commit_file` give the same view of a single commit compared with its
parent.

``` python
review = repo.review('main', 'claude/ramabana-branching-review-uqj6v2')
review['summary'], review['commits']

file_review = repo.review_file('main', 'claude/ramabana-branching-review-uqj6v2', review['files'][0]['path'])
file_review['left'], file_review['right'], file_review['patch']
```

## Build a library pipeline

For anything
[`uv_ci`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/workflow.html#uv_ci) does
not cover, start from `Workflow(name)`, add triggers through `.on`, and
add jobs. gheasy has one-call presets for common jobs. `uv_lint_job`
adds a `lint` job that runs ruff. `uv_test_job` adds a `test` job that
runs pytest. `uv_pypi_job` adds a `publish` job that builds the package
and uploads it to PyPI. `needs` names the job that must pass first.
`build()` turns the builder into a document you can print or save.

The `publish` job runs only when a GitHub release starts the workflow.
This example triggers on pushes and pull requests only. Add
`.release(types=['published'])` to the triggers to publish on release.

``` python
from gheasy.workflow import Workflow

wfb = Workflow("ci")
wfb.on.push(branches=["main"]).pull_request()
wfb.uv_lint_job()
wfb.uv_test_job(needs="lint")
wfb.uv_pypi_job(needs="test")
print(wfb.build().to_yaml())
```

    name: ci
    on:
      push:
        branches:
          - main
      pull_request:
    jobs:
      lint:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - name: Checkout
            uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - name: Setup uv
            uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
          - name: Install dependencies
            run: uv sync --frozen
          - name: Lint
            run: uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .
      test:
        needs: lint
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - name: Checkout
            uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - name: Setup uv
            uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
          - name: Install dependencies
            run: uv sync --frozen
          - name: Test
            run: uv run pytest
      publish:
        needs: test
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        if: github.event_name == 'release'
        permissions:
          id-token: write
        steps:
          - name: Checkout
            uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - name: Setup uv
            uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
          - name: Build
            run: uv build
          - name: Publish
            uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1

## Build an application pipeline

When no preset fits, build the job step by step. `job(name)` starts a
job. `needs` makes it wait for another job. `runs_on` sets the machine
it runs on. A step helper such as `checkout` or `setup_uv` adds one step
and returns that step. `end_step()` returns to the job so you can add
the next step. `end_job()` returns to the workflow. This example tests
every push to
[`main`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#main) and then
deploys to Fly.io.

``` python
wfb = Workflow("deploy")
wfb.on.push(branches=["main"])

wfb.uv_test_job()

wfb.job("deploy").needs("test").runs_on("ubuntu-latest")\
    .checkout().end_step()\
    .setup_uv().end_step()\
    .step("Deploy to Fly.io").run("fly deploy --remote-only").end_job()

print(wfb.build().to_yaml())
```

    name: deploy
    on:
      push:
        branches:
          - main
    jobs:
      test:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - name: Checkout
            uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - name: Setup uv
            uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
          - name: Install dependencies
            run: uv sync --frozen
          - name: Test
            run: uv run pytest
      deploy:
        needs: test
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - name: Checkout
            uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - name: Setup uv
            uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
          - name: Deploy to Fly.io
            run: fly deploy --remote-only

## Configure LFS and secrets

Git LFS keeps large binary files out of the Git history and commits a
small pointer file in their place.
[`gh_lfs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_lfs)
installs LFS in the repository and tracks the file patterns you pass. It
also saves the patterns to `.gheasy/config.json` unless you pass
`persist=False`. With no patterns it tracks a default list of model and
data file types.

GitHub Actions jobs read their settings from secrets, which GitHub
encrypts and hides in logs, and from variables, which are plain text.
[`gh_push_env`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_push_env)
takes a dict of values and sends each key as a secret or a variable, as
the `env_schema` in `.gheasy/config.json` says. A key whose schema
default is `None` becomes a secret. A key with a string default becomes
a variable. A key missing from the schema is skipped with a warning.
[`gh_push_env`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_push_env)
raises `FileNotFoundError` when `.gheasy/config.json` does not exist. It
sets the values with the `gh` command line tool, which must be installed
and logged in.

``` python
from gheasy.core import gh_lfs, gh_secrets_from_file, gh_push_env, GheasyConfig

gh_lfs(['*.mp3', '*.ogg', '*.wav', '*.png', '*.jpg', '*.webp', '*.xml', '*.db'])

cfg = GheasyConfig(app='vedicreader', env_schema={
    # variables: string defaults
    'MODE': 'dev', 'PORT': '5001', 'DOMAIN': 'http://localhost:5001',
    'WANT_GOOGLE': 'true', 'WANT_GIT': 'false',
    'NEED_BACKUP': 'false', 'RC_TYPE': 's3', 'RC_PROVIDER': 'Cloudflare',
    # secrets: None defaults
    'JWT_SCRT': None, 'RESEND_API_KEY': None,
    'GOOGLE_CLI': None, 'GOOGLE_SCRT': None,
    'CF_ACCESS_KEY_ID': None, 'CF_SCRT_ACCESS_KEY': None, 'CF_ENDPOINT': None,
})
cfg.save()

import os
gh_push_env(dict(os.environ))
```

When every value is a secret, the schema is not needed.
[`gh_secrets_from_file`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_secrets_from_file)
reads the `KEY=VALUE` lines of a file such as `.env`, ignores blank
lines and `#` comments, and sets each value as a GitHub secret.
`dry_run=True` prints the `gh` commands and does not run them.
`env='prod'` scopes the secrets to the `prod` environment.

``` python
gh_secrets_from_file('.env')

gh_secrets_from_file('.env', dry_run=True)
```

## Build a cross-package pipeline

A step can run any shell command, including Python that imports another
package. This workflow uses
[dockeasy](https://github.com/Karthik777/dockeasy) to write a
Dockerfile. It then builds the image and pushes it to GHCR, GitHub’s
container registry. The `paths` filter starts the workflow on a push
only when one of the files that generate the Dockerfile has changed.
`workflow_dispatch` adds a button to run the workflow by hand from the
repository’s Actions tab. `with_` sets the inputs of an action.

``` python
wfb = Workflow("Build caddy-sqlite image")
wfb.on.push(branches=["main"], paths=["dockeasy/proxy.py", "nbs/01_proxy.ipynb"])
wfb.on.workflow_dispatch()

wfb.job("build-and-push").runs_on("ubuntu-latest")\
    .permissions(contents="read", packages="write")\
    .checkout().end_step()\
    .setup_uv().end_step()\
    .step("Install deps").run("uv sync").end_step()\
    .step("Generate Dockerfile").run(
        'uv run python -c "\n'
        'from dockeasy.proxy import caddy_sqlite_dockerfile\n'
        'caddy_sqlite_dockerfile().save(\'Dockerfile\')\n'
        '"'
    ).end_step()\
    .step("Log in to GHCR").uses("docker/login-action@v3")\
        .with_(registry="ghcr.io",
               username="${{ github.actor }}",
               password="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}").end_step()\
    .step("Build and push").uses("docker/build-push-action@v5")\
        .with_(context=".", push=True,
               tags="ghcr.io/vedicreader/caddy-sqlite:latest").end_job()

print(wfb.build().to_yaml())
```

    name: Build caddy-sqlite image
    on:
      push:
        branches:
          - main
        paths:
          - dockeasy/proxy.py
          - nbs/01_proxy.ipynb
      workflow_dispatch:
    jobs:
      build-and-push:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: read
          packages: write
        steps:
          - name: Checkout
            uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - name: Setup uv
            uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
          - name: Install deps
            run: uv sync
          - name: Generate Dockerfile
            run: "uv run python -c \"\nfrom dockeasy.proxy import caddy_sqlite_dockerfile\ncaddy_sqlite_dockerfile().save('Dockerfile')\n\
              \""
          - name: Log in to GHCR
            uses: docker/login-action@v3
            with:
              registry: ghcr.io
              username: ${{ github.actor }}
              password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          - name: Build and push
            uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
            with:
              context: .
              push: true
              tags: ghcr.io/vedicreader/caddy-sqlite:latest
